places.name: Ngư Lương Trấn
places.size: A walled river-mouth town of about 6,000 people: about 1,300 grey roofs inside a wall about 600 m across, with a zigzag fish weir of stone and bamboo about 700 m long and some 40 boats.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), grassland coast at sea level, a plain river spilling into the sea, a port. Held by Lạc Hà Tông; weirs came to the plain in 430. Nearest: forest Bạch Du Lâm (125 km), villages Phương Thảo Thôn (158 km) and Vãn Đăng Thôn (168 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Low sun on a run of silver fish: the weir's traps glint in a long zigzag and a family in waders lifts out a trap.
places.subject: The place: Ngư Lương Trấn, the Fish Weir Town, at a river mouth. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle in the late morning; two lobes of forested gold-green hills with farm plots at the left meet at a river mouth opening to the sea, a second river entering at the top. The river is a wide plain river of brown-green water, spreading into a pale estuary. The town: a small walled rectangle of grey stone with four gates and a water gate, about thirteen hundred grey-tile roofs in orderly lanes, a fish market with long stalls, smoke houses with thin plumes, a net-loft, a boat yard with three hulls on slips, a plain grey hall of the ruling sect and a little hall of the weir elders; about forty boats at a stone quay. Signature element: across the whole river mouth runs a great zigzag weir of stone and bamboo, about seven hundred paces long, its long arrow-shaped arms folding back and forth across the water with a gap at each point for a trap basket; hundreds of woven traps full of silver fish glint along it; each stretch has a family's rough shelter at its end, with a fish-rack, and people in waders lift out the traps; one section is being rebuilt, with raw bamboo bright against old grey stone. Life at scale: hundreds of tiny fishers along the weir. Light: bright warm late-morning light from the upper left, glittering water, long short shadows beneath the weir.

places.name: Điền Viên Thôn
places.size: A village of gardens and fields of about 250 people: about 50 houses each in its own walled garden, with round moon gates, orchards and fields spread over about 800 m.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), grassland on the coast at 0.02 km, a port in a small way. Held by Mục Vân Trang, feeding the scholars of Nhạn Thanh Thành who retire here. Nearest: spirit vein Ẩn Canh Mạch (75 km), ruin Di Hà Trấn (112 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A soft afternoon: an old scholar sits in a study seen through a round moon gate, writing a herder's letter and waiting for his payment in vegetables.
places.subject: The place: Điền Viên Thôn, the Fields and Gardens Village, a village of retired scholars. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a gentle afternoon; a lobed grassy coast of gold-green hills and dark groves, the sea to the north and west. The village: about fifty grey-tile houses, each standing in its own walled garden, the walls low, whitewashed and neat, and in nearly every wall a round moon gate; through the gates, glimpsed from above, the courtyards with a tree, a rock, a small pond and a small study with a window open to the garden; narrow lanes of pale stone between the walls, a shared well, a little stone bridge over an irrigation channel, a modest hall for gatherings, and a long storehouse where the scholars' vegetables are weighed. Signature element: the moon gates, about forty round white-rimmed openings in the garden walls, each a small perfect circle seen from above in a row like a string of coins; scholars in pale robes sit tending vegetables, a few at desks near open windows, and herder visitors on horses wait at one gate. Life at scale: a peaceful settled place, small, ordered, productive. Light: soft warm afternoon light from the upper left, shadows of the fruit trees on the walls, blossoms drifting. Pear and peach trees stand in the walled gardens in pink and white bloom, and in the lanes a few hens and a sleeping dog lie in the sun beside stacked baskets of beans and cabbages.

places.name: Yến Quy Thôn
places.size: A small farm village of about 140 people: about 30 grey-roofed houses gathered around one old farmstead; the old farm's roof ridge carries about 100 clay swallows.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), grassland on the coast at 0.02 km, a port in a small way. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Named by 300 after swallows that returned to the same farm every spring. Nearest: hot spring Yến Ngữ Thang (90 km), city Thảo Đường Thành (160 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Early spring: the first real swallows are back and sit between the clay ones along the old ridge, and a child counts them.
places.subject: The place: Yến Quy Thôn, the Swallows' Return Village, around one old farm. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a clear spring morning; a lobed grassy coast of gold-green hills and dark groves, the sea to the north. The village: about thirty grey-tile houses gathered in a loose ring around one very old farmstead, a long low farmhouse of thick whitewashed walls and a deep grey roof, with a courtyard, a barn, a well and a great pear tree; each of the other houses has a small yard, a pig-pen and a vegetable plot, and narrow paths lead between them; a plain granary and a small shrine of piled stone. Signature element: the old farm's long roof ridge, lined end to end with about a hundred little clay swallows, each made by a different family, pale grey, white and brown, forming a long row like beads; among the clay birds sit about a dozen real swallows, nearly the same size, with a few more darting around the eaves. A family on the doorstep looks up. Life at scale: a plain, small, rooted place, a few figures in the fields, hens and a dog in the yards. Light: soft golden morning light from the upper left, a thin mist over the fields, gentle shadows. In the farmyards below the ridge, ducks dabble in a small pond, a cart stands with its shafts down, and a line of washing hangs between two pear trees, small signs of a household that has been here a hundred years.

places.name: Chu Tân Thôn
places.size: A ferry village of about 160 people: about 35 low houses on wet shore land below high-tide level, two tall carved ferry posts, a rope ferry, and a few boats.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), grassland at -0.05 km, a low wet shore below the level of the sea at high tide, a port. Held by Mục Vân Trang, whose herds cross here every spring. Nearest: hot spring Ôn Tân Trì (79 km), spirit vein Trì Vân Mạch (135 km), town Thanh Điền Trấn (190 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: High tide: a flat barge crawls along the rope across the creek with three horses on it, and the ferryman calls each horse by name.
places.subject: The place: Chu Tân Thôn, the Boat Ford Village, on a low wet shore. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at high tide in the early morning; a lobed grassy coast of gold-green hills and dark groves, the sea to the west and north. The shore is wet and low, with salt grass, mudflats half under water at high tide and dry old river-bed lines scarred across it. The village: about thirty-five low grey-tile and thatched houses raised on mounds of earth and on short stilts, joined by plank walks, each with a boat tied at the door; a ferrymen's hall, a net-loft, hay barns with horse corrals, and a small lamp-tower. Signature element: at the old ford two very tall carved ferry posts, each carved with waves and a horse's head, stand on either side of a narrow tidal creek, joined by one heavy rope across the water, and along the rope a flat barge crawls with a few horses and travellers on it; on the near bank a herd of about forty horses waits to cross, tiny and various in colour, and ferrymen with poles stand at the water's edge. Life at scale: a quiet, damp, patient ferry stop. Light: gentle gold early-morning light from the upper left, soft haze over the mudflats, water gleaming. Behind the village a few reed-cutters' paths run out across the salt grass toward the dry old river bed, and wading birds stand along the water's edge in a thin line, indifferent to the ferrymen.

places.name: Lô Cảng Thôn
places.size: A watch village of about 170 people: about 35 reed-thatched boat sheds and houses round a sheltered reed harbour about 300 m across, with a tall timber watchtower.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), grassland on the coast at 0.01 km, a port, a sheltered reed harbour. Held by Lạc Hà Tông, which built its western watch here in 800. Nearest: hot spring Hàn Thú Thang (112 km), ruin Dã Độ Trấn (125 km), city Thảo Đường Thành (158 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Dawn: the tower's sunset-red banner stirs over the reeds, and a watchman climbs the ladder to look at a strange sail on the horizon.
places.subject: The place: Lô Cảng Thôn, the Reed Harbour Village, a watch post on a sheltered harbour. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dawn; a bay bites into gold-green hills with dark groves and a patch of farm plots, a stream reaching the water at the lower right. The village: about thirty-five boat sheds and small houses thatched with reed in pale gold, standing on short piles along the reed edge and on a low gravel spit, joined by plank walks; about twenty narrow coast boats under the sheds or tied at little landings; net racks, a smoking shed, a well; a larger plain hall for the watch with a small barracks. Signature element: out of the reeds rises a tall timber watchtower, about thirty paces high, braced with cross-beams, with a railed platform at the top where a small signal fire basket stands cold, and from its mast flies a long sunset-red banner without a symbol; watchmen and fishers mix tiny on the plank walks; a pair of watch-boats lie ready at the harbour mouth. Life at scale: a modest working village with a vigilant eye on the sea. Light: first rosy dawn light from the upper left, mist rising off the reeds, the red banner the one strong colour. At the harbour mouth a small causeway of stacked reeds and stone shelters the inner basin, and children in shallow-draught punts race along the reed lanes while the watch changes at the foot of the tower.

places.name: Diêm Điền Thôn
places.size: A salt-makers' village of about 200 people: about 40 low houses at the edge of a glittering grid of about 400 salt pans spread over about 3 km along the coast, with rows of salt cones.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), grassland on the flat west coast at 0.01 km, a port in a small way. Held by Lạc Hà Tông; pans dug in 200 made the continent's first sea salt. Nearest: hot spring Hàm Thủy Thang (79 km), ruin Triều Một Trấn (158 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: A hot dry noon: the pans are blinding white and pink, and tiny rakers draw the salt into shining cones in long rows.
places.subject: The place: Diêm Điền Thôn, the Salt Pans Village, at the edge of a vast grid of salt pans. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at noon; a broad land of tawny grass and green hills lies beside a small bay, farm plots at the right and dark forest on the heights. Between the squares of pans and the hills a west coast with a bright blue sea shows at the top; shallow square pans in clear glassy blue, rose and pure white stretch inland and along the coast in a huge glittering grid, edged with low pale mud banks and channels fed from the sea through small sluice gates. The village: about forty low grey-tile and thatched houses with flat drying roofs at the pans' edge, a long salt warehouse with a pale roof, a boiling house with a thin plume, a cart yard with salt wagons, a small harbour with salt barges. Signature element: between the shallow squares stand long rows of shining salt cones, hundreds, glittering white as snow, raked up by hand by tiny workers with wide wooden rakes; one pan in the first row stands apart, fenced with a low wooden rail, unused and spotless, with a tiny handful of white at its centre. Life at scale: a hot dazzling work-place where the figures are small black dots among white. Light: hard bright noon light from the upper left, strong glare, colours of the pans glowing, short crisp shadows of the cones.

places.name: Phù Chử Đảo
places.size: A natural site: a low wooded isle about 3 km across with a few dozen egg-gatherers' huts at most, circled by a dense raft of thousands of wild ducks about 400 m wide.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), temperate forest isle off the plain coast at 0.01 km; no sect holds it; only egg-gatherers go ashore in spring. Nearest: beast lair Hải Báo Chử (202 km), village Lật Thụ Thôn (206 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A calm spring dawn: a boat idles at the edge of the duck raft, waiting for it to part, and from above the water looks feathered.
places.subject: The place: Phù Chử Đảo, the Isle of the Wild Ducks, a low wooded isle in a calm sea. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dawn on a flat calm day; a scatter of low forested islets lies in a calm open sea, this one the largest, heart-shaped and dark green, with two smaller isles to its west and a rocky coast far off in the corner. A calm, still, pale blue-grey sea with a faint pink glow fills the frame, with a thin mist rising from the water; the isle is about three kilometres across, thickly covered with dark broad-leaved trees and a few pines, with a narrow pale beach and a small muddy cove. Around it floats a thick, shifting raft of wild ducks, thousands upon thousands, brown, green-necked and white, so dense that the water looks feathered, in a ring about four hundred paces wide, with swirling patterns where flocks move. Signature element: the duck raft itself and, at the edge of it, a single small fishing boat waiting, its crew sitting patiently, since anyone who forces a way through will have no luck all season; on the beach of the cove a small camp of three huts of egg-gatherers with a thread of smoke and a stack of baskets, and tiny figures at the tree line. Life at scale: a quiet wild place that people wait on. Light: soft pink and gold dawn light from the upper left, a gentle mist, calm reflections of the trees.

places.name: Tịch Chiếu Đảo
places.size: A natural site: a small mountainous island about 20 km long in the open sea, snow on its summits, a long stone bench on the western cliff, about 60 small cairns on the grass below; at most a landing and one boat.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), the westernmost island, last land to see the sunset of Lạc Hà. On the map it is a long narrow mountainous island with a bare grey ridge, snowfields on its summits, forested flanks, and three small rocky islets near it, in open sea. Nearest: spirit vein Hỏa Ngọc Mạch (224 km), town Chung Phàm Trấn (403 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Sunset: an elder sits alone on the long stone bench facing the red sea, and below the cliff the boat that brought her is already rowing away.
places.subject: The place: Tịch Chiếu Đảo, the Isle of the Evening Glow, the westernmost island. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at sunset; a mountainous island, long and narrow, runs from upper left to lower right, its spine a ridge of bare grey rock with white snowfields on the highest summits, green forest and grass on its lower flanks, a steep dark cliff on its western side and a small gravel landing on a sheltered eastern shore, three small rocky islets off it. Evening gold and red light lies in long bands over the deep blue sea. The island: no village, no wall, no hall; the grass is short and wind-combed and dotted with small cairns of grey stones, about sixty of them, each a knee-high pile, scattered thinly and then more thickly toward the western cliff. Signature element: on the very edge of the western cliff stands a single long stone bench, pale grey, about twelve paces long, facing the setting sun, with one tiny figure seated in an elder's grey robe, alone; a thin trodden path leads from the landing across the grass to the bench. At the landing a single small boat is already pulling away, a speck, leaving a thin white wake across the dark water. Life at scale: a tiny silent place at the edge of the world, the loneliest picture in the set. Light: the low red-gold sunset light from the upper left casting long shadows of the cairns, the sea glowing, a deep blue sky to the east.

places.name: Lạc Nhạn Hồ
places.size: A natural site: a long narrow lake about 30 km from end to end in rugged rust-orange coastal hills, thousands of wild geese on it and its shore; at most a few reed hides for goose-watchers.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), grassland at sea level; on the map a narrow lake in a fold of rugged rust-orange hills near the coast, a stream running to the sea, no sect holds it. A goose sect (Nhạn Trận Môn) is tied to the geese. Nearest: city Nhạn Thanh Thành (168 km), beast lair Hắc Thứu Đài (320 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Autumn dusk: the first V of geese lowers onto the lake in long lines and the whole shore is white with birds.
places.subject: The place: Lạc Nhạn Hồ, the Lake Where the Geese Alight, a long narrow lake in rugged coastal hills. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dusk in autumn; a long narrow blue lake lies in a fold of rugged hills of rust-orange rock and tawny grass dotted with dark conifer groves, a stream leaving its southern end to meet the sea a short way off. Signature element: the geese, a whole living landscape of birds; on one shore a few small reed hides, three or four low huts of woven reed, in which tiny figures watch, and a short row of stakes in the water. No buildings beyond the hides, no roofline. Life at scale: an enormous quiet gathering, birds like grains of flour. Light: warm amber dusk light from the upper left on the reeds and the water, long soft shadows, the sky glowing at the horizon. The whole lake is wide silver water ringed by pale reed beds; the geese float in dense mats and walk in grey-white flocks along the mud, so many that the shore looks stitched, and their long evening calls rise over the water in an unbroken cry. A narrow stream leaves its southern end, carrying the lake's overflow past a thread of green marsh toward the sea. On the nearest shore a few low reed hides stand on stilts, and in the shallows a short row of stakes marks where goose-watchers wade out each dawn; the rust-orange hills behind the lake glow warm against the pale water, and the evening calls of the flocks carry over the whole fold of the land.

places.name: Nhạn Trận Môn
places.size: A minor drill-sect of about 60 disciples in files of five and ten: a walled compound of about 45 buildings, about 250 m across, laid out in an exact goose-formation V, with a great drill ground.
places.where: Region 11 (Trường Thiên Nguyên), steppe on the coast at 0.07 km. Vassal of Lạc Hà Tông, righteous. Twelve tiles from Nhạn Thanh Thành. Nearest: Nhạn Thanh Thành (301 km), town Thanh Phong Trấn (320 km), spirit vein Nhất Sắc Mạch (382 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Morning drill: sixty disciples in white and grey move in a living V across the great yard, their shadows pointing the same way.
places.subject: The place: Nhạn Trận Môn, the Gate of the Goose Formation, a drilling sect on the open steppe. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a clear morning; a coastal ridge of rust-orange and green hills runs above the sea, a narrow lake and a stream reaching the sea to its east. The sect: a walled compound of about forty-five buildings of grey stone and grey tile, laid out so that, seen from above, the whole compound forms a vast V like a flying goose formation, the two arms of the V made of long matching barracks and halls, each arm of ten identical halls stepping back along a line, converging at a tall gate-tower at the V's point which faces the sea; between the arms lies an enormous drill ground of packed pale earth, about two hundred paces by a hundred, marked with lines in white lime. Signature element: on the drill ground, sixty tiny disciples in grey and white move in perfect files of five and ten, forming a living V that matches the V of the buildings, their shadows all falling the same way; at the point of the V a taller figure, the master, with a long staff. Behind the arms, a kitchen court, a granary, a small shrine and a few houses of the mortal servants. Life at scale: a spare, severe, geometric place of discipline, smaller than a city block. Light: clear gold morning light from the upper left, long exact shadows of the halls, every line crisp.

places.name: Thiên Bảo Trai
places.size: A refiners' minor sect of about 70 members and twice as many hired hands: a tall seat of about 80 buildings on a steppe rise about 500 m across, with a ring of about 20 refining furnaces; it is the richest of the minor sects.
places.where: Region 12 (the bay), steppe at 0.4 km on a rugged rust-red upland with grey rock crests and a tarn (no sea in the crop). Founded 350 as a refiners' workshop; sworn to Lạc Hà Tông. It runs the treasure auction each season and sits beside the market Vật Hoa Thị. Nearest: spirit vein Long Quang Mạch (79 km), mine Xích Kim Khoáng (152 km), ruin Vô Định Thành (158 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Evening: the gilt-bronze ridges burn in the setting sun and the furnace smoke trails green, copper and violet.
places.subject: The place: Thiên Bảo Trai, the Treasure Studio, a rich artifact-refining sect on a dry upland rise among red ridges. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at evening; a rugged dry upland of rust-red and ochre ridges and folded hills with tawny grass in the hollows, grey-white rocky crests along the right edge and a tiny blue tarn among them, a small stream in the lower left, no sea in the frame. The sect: about eighty buildings stacked in six tiers up the rise inside a stout grey wall, stacked pagoda roofs of grey tile each ridged in gilt bronze that burns in the evening sun, climbing to a tall central tower, the highest outline; courtyards of auction halls with screened booths, appraisers' offices, strong-rooms with iron doors, steward's quarters, apprentices' dormitories, and a great court where the quarterly auction is held with its hundred screened seats. Signature element: around the base of the rise runs a ring of about twenty refining furnaces, each a tall squat brick chimney with a bronze cap, trailing thin smoke in green, copper and violet colours that drift together and hang in a faint coloured haze over the sect; around the furnaces slag heaps, ore carts, stacks of ingots and crates of finished artifacts. A road runs down to the market below. Life at scale: several hundred tiny figures, refiners in aprons, hired hands with carts, appraisers in grey. Light: strong red-gold evening light from the upper left on the gilt ridges, long shadows.

places.name: Tử Điện Thành
places.size: A walled bay port city of about 40,000 people: strong walls about 2.2 km on a side, some 9,000 packed grey roofs, a tall violet-roofed armoury tower, a harbour with about 70 vessels.
places.where: Region 12 (the bay), grassland coast at sea level at a river mouth, a port. Founded by Lạc Anh Phái in 360; taken by Lạc Hà Tông in 620 and renamed for its armoury. Nearest: ruin Kim Cốc Thành (135 km), village Hải Môn Thôn (180 km), beast lair Độc Phong Nguyên (190 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: A clear evening: the faint violet shimmer of the ward array lies over the whole city, and the armoury tower's violet tile glows like lightning held still.
places.subject: The place: Tử Điện Thành, the City of the Purple Lightning, a heavily walled port at a river mouth on the bay. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a clear evening; a river with several branches comes down through green farmland hills to the shore of a wide bay at the upper left, farm plots in the south. The coast is bright with farm plots near the shore and the river's branches shine in the evening light. The city: strong grey stone walls about two and a quarter kilometres on a side, thick and high with square towers every fifty paces and a double gate, enclosing about nine thousand grey-tile roofs packed tight in disciplined grid streets: smiths' quarters with rows of forges and chimneys, barracks and drill yards, wide guild courts, a harbour with about seventy vessels at a stone quay, warehouses, and a hall of the ruling sect; in many courtyards a peach tree. Signature element: above the roofs rises a tall armoury tower of seven tiers, roofed in violet-glazed tile that gleams like lightning, the tallest outline for kilometres; over the whole city hangs the faint violet shimmer of the ward array, a thin dome of pale violet light with a delicate geometry of lines in it, glowing against the dusk; lines of tiny guards in matching grey march along the walls. Life at scale: tens of thousands of residents, disciplined smiths and guards. Light: gold-violet evening light from the upper left, long shadows, the shimmer pale against the sky.

places.name: Vật Hoa Thị
places.size: A great open market of about 3,000 stalls and about 10,000 traders and visitors on a market day, around a central square about 200 m across; a town-sized tented market about 1.5 km across with about 250 permanent shops.
places.where: Region 12 (the bay), steppe at 0.15 km below Thiên Bảo Trai, dry. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Founded 500; sells what the Trai refines and what the bay digs, grows and catches. Nearest: beast lair Hạt Vĩ Cương (106 km), spirit vein Ốc Thổ Mạch (190 km), Thiên Bảo Trai (202 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: A market-day noon: a deal is being weighed on the great steelyard and the whole crowd leans in to see the needle settle.
places.subject: The place: Vật Hoa Thị, the Market of the Land's Riches, a vast open market on dry steppe. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at noon on a clear day; a wide dry hollow among rust-red and ochre badland ridges and tawny grass slopes, grey stony crests along the right edge, a thin stream and a little pool at the lower left, a road coming down from a rise at the top. Dry tan and rust slopes frame the market, and the pale road is dusty. The market: about three thousand stalls under awnings of every colour, red, ochre, indigo, white and green, in dense radiating rows around a large central square, with about two hundred and fifty permanent shops of grey brick and tile along the main avenues, auction booths, caravanserais with stables and wagons, animal pens, food courts with smoke, weighing sheds, and rows of camels and carts at the edge; stalls sell refined artifacts, ingots, pills, silk, salt, fish, grain and spirit herbs. Signature element: in the central square stands a great bronze steelyard on a stone frame, taller than a house, its long beam and huge pans glinting green-bronze, where any trader may have goods weighed in public; a crowd of about a thousand tiny figures ringed around it. An alchemist's pill-stall with a bright red awning stands at one corner. Life at scale: a dense, loud, shifting multitude, ten thousand figures in colour. Light: bright noon light from the upper left, colourful awnings casting sharp small shadows, dust haze glowing gold.

places.name: Liễu Ngạn Trấn
places.size: A small walled river town of about 4,500 people: about 1,000 roofs behind a high earthen levee about 1.5 km long, with a stone flood-pillar about 6 m tall and several hundred willows.
places.where: Region 12 (the bay), grassland at 0.01 km on a river through flat grassland, no coast shown. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Willows planted in 410 to hold the river. Nearest: ruin Hồng Vũ Thành (125 km), beast lair Bạch Miết Chử (125 km), village Khê Thanh Thôn (158 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: Flood season: the river climbs the pillar toward the red mark, the drum is beating, and a line of tiny people carry sandbags along the levee.
places.subject: The place: Liễu Ngạn Trấn, the Willow Bank Town, a small walled town on a river through green hills, behind a levee. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at high water in the afternoon; green hills with a river junction and a long narrow lake in the north, a rugged sea coast at the left, farm plots and darker forest to the east. The brown river is swollen and fast, spilling grey-brown water into low fields beyond the levee. The town: a small walled square of grey stone and tile behind a high earthen levee about fifteen hundred paces long, covered with grass and lined along both banks with several hundred long willows with trailing pale-green branches; about a thousand grey-tile roofs in neat blocks inside the wall, a small market square, granaries on raised stone feet, a boat shed and a quay, a plain hall. Signature element: on the levee stands a tall stone flood-pillar, about six paces tall, cut with ring-marks of every great flood, the highest painted red, with the river's water now climbing near the red band; a large drum on a frame beside it with a drummer; and a long line of about two hundred tiny people, one from each household, carrying sandbags and baskets of earth along the levee top to a weak point where a seep darkens the grass. Life at scale: a river-bound town on watch and in motion. Light: low amber afternoon light from the upper left, the brown water gleaming, willow shadows long.

places.name: Hòa Phong Trấn
places.size: A small port town of about 6,000 people: about 1,400 low airy roofs, each with a tall woven wind-scoop, along about 900 m of the open bay shore, with a small harbour of about 40 boats.
places.where: Region 12 (the bay), grassland coast at 0.01 km, a port on the open bay. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. In 900, the year of the southern plague, a sea breeze kept it free of fever, so it is a refuge for the sick. Nearest: spirit vein Huệ Phong Mạch (100 km), village Tân Khẩu Thôn (202 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A bright breezy morning: all the wind-scoops on the roofs turn together toward the sea, and convalescents in white sit on a long terrace in the sun.
places.subject: The place: Hòa Phong Trấn, the Gentle Breeze Town, a port town that leans into the sea breeze. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright breezy morning; a green hilly coast with farm plots on its slopes, a river entering the bay at the top, the open bay to the north. Small crisp wavelets and a few white sails dot the bay, and a light cloud drifts overhead. The town: about fourteen hundred low airy grey-tile roofs in open rows along the shore, with wide lanes and courtyards left open so that air may pass; on every roof stands a tall woven wind-scoop, a conical or hooded basket-frame of pale reed, its open mouth turned to the sea, so the whole town seems to lean into the breeze like a field of tilted hats; a harbour of about forty small boats at a pier, a market, a long convalescent terrace with rows of reclining chairs of pale cane, a healers' hall with herb gardens, and a few plain inns. Signature element: the wind-scoops, about fourteen hundred of them, a forest of reed cones all pointing the same way; on the long terrace some two hundred tiny convalescents in white sit in the sun. Life at scale: a quiet, gentle, healing town. Gulls wheel over the harbour and the smell of salt and healing herbs hangs over the lanes. Light: bright clean morning light from the upper left, small crisp shadows of the scoops, the water sparkling.

places.name: Ngũ Cốc Thành
places.size: A grain-trade port city of about 45,000 people: walls about 2.5 km on a side, some 10,000 roofs, and a waterfront row of five great round grain towers each about 40 m tall, with a harbour of about 90 vessels.
places.where: Region 12 (the bay), grassland coast at 0.01 km, a port. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Grew rich on the trade lost when Kim Cốc Viên burned; many merchants are Kim Cốc families. Nearest: beast lair Thạc Thử Cương (103 km), hot spring Vong Ưu Tuyền (293 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: A busy harbour morning: grain pours down the wooden chutes into the holds of waiting ships, and each guild's flag colour is on its tower.
places.subject: The place: Ngũ Cốc Thành, the Five Grains City, a rich walled grain port on the bay. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright morning; a straight green hilly coast with small farm plots, the open bay to the north and dark forest at the lower right. The city: grey stone walls about two and a half kilometres on a side, gates on the landward sides and a long harbour front; inside, about ten thousand grey-tile roofs in guild districts, each with its own court, scales and counting house; a great exchange hall at the centre, cart-yards with long lines of grain wagons, rice mills, barley mills, mills with water wheels, brewers' yards, a hall of the ruling sect, the mansions of old Kim Cốc merchant families with high gate roofs. A harbour of about ninety vessels, big grain ships and barges, at a stone waterfront. Signature element: along the waterfront stands a row of five tall round grain towers, each about forty paces high, each roofed differently for its grain, one with a golden thatch cone for millet, one with a green-glazed dome for rice, one with a red-tile cone for wheat, one with a grey slate cap for barley, one with a flat white roof for beans; from each runs a wooden chute down to the ships, with grain pouring like pale water. Life at scale: tens of thousands of tiny dockers, carters and clerks. Light: warm gold morning light from the upper left, dust of grain glowing in the air.

places.name: Khê Thanh Thôn
places.size: A brook village of about 180 people: about 40 grey roofs strung along 600 m of a clear brook, with a row of about 12 small covered rinsing sheds on stilts over the water.
places.where: Region 12 (the bay), grassland at 0.02 km on a clear brook, no coast shown. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Since 700, Thiên Bảo Trai has washed its finest refinings here. Nearest: spirit vein Chu Hoa Mạch (79 km), town Liễu Ngạn Trấn (158 km), beast lair Bạch Miết Chử (168 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: Morning: refiners' apprentices in grey carry covered baskets down to the sheds, and the brook chatters loudly under them.
places.subject: The place: Khê Thanh Thôn, the Brook Sound Village, on a very clear grassland brook. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright morning; green hills where a long narrow lake feeds streams that meet a river, rust-red ridges to the north and the sea at the upper left. The brook runs diagonally through the frame, its stony bed visible and ripples white where it chatters over stones. The village: about forty grey-tile houses with whitewashed walls strung along both banks, each with a small garden and a footbridge or stepping stones; a small hall for the keeper of the banks; fences that keep cattle back from the water and a stretch of banks laid in clean stone; a wash-house, a shrine of piled stones. Signature element: over the brook stand a row of about twelve small covered rinsing sheds on stilts, each a little square roof of grey tile on four posts straddling the water, with a platform and baskets inside, where the water chatters loudly over the stones beneath; apprentices of the artifact sect in grey, about twenty tiny figures, carry covered baskets of finished pieces down a well-trodden path; metal glints under the water. Life at scale: a small clean quiet village whose work is keeping a stream pure. A few ducks float below the sheds, and the path to the water is worn smooth by apprentices' feet. Light: clear bright light from the upper left, the water sparkling, shadows of the sheds on the stones.

places.name: Khê Đầu Thôn
places.size: A small spring village of about 100 people: about 22 grey-roofed houses around a round stone basin about 8 m across at the head of a brook; the spring is guarded like a shrine.
places.where: Region 12 (the bay), grassland at 0.01 km where a brook rises from the ground, no coast shown. Held by Lạc Hà Tông; upstream of Khê Thanh. Its water is the clearest. Nearest: beast lair Độc Phong Nguyên (90 km), ruin Hồng Vũ Thành (158 km), beast lair Bạch Miết Chử (177 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: Dawn: the carp-headed spout pours into the round basin and the brook begins from the overflow; no one washes above the basin's lip.
places.subject: The place: Khê Đầu Thôn, the Brook Head Village, where a brook rises. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dawn; green hills below a long narrow lake whose headwater streams meet a river running down to a bay at the left. A silver thread of brook runs away from the spring, widening as small feeders join, with open dewy grass around the village. The village: about twenty-two small grey-tile houses with whitewashed walls clustered close around the spring in a ring, each with a small garden of green vegetables and a low stone wall, narrow paths of white stones leading to the spring; a small plain hall; a neat grassy square. Signature element: at the centre, a round stone basin about eight paces across, ringed with pale stones, fed by a stone spout carved as a carp's head from which clear water pours in a thin, bright, curved stream; from the basin's overflow the brook begins through a notched stone lip; around the basin a low railed fence with a gate, like a shrine, and a small stone lantern; downstream, below the village, a few people wash on stepping stones, well below the basin. About fifteen tiny villagers, two guarding at the gate. Life at scale: a tiny, reverent hamlet at a source. Light: soft clear pink-gold dawn light from the upper left, dew sparkling on the grass, the water pale and bright. A single narrow plank footbridge crosses below the basin, and the village's washing-steps, stone ledges at the water's edge, lie well downstream where the stream has already grown wide and noisy.

places.name: Hải Môn Thôn
places.size: A fishing village of about 200 people: about 40 houses along a bay shore beside a great natural rock arch about 40 m high and 30 m wide, with about 25 boats.
places.where: Region 12 (the bay), grassland coast at sea level, a port in a small way. Held by Lạc Hà Tông. Named since 450 for the Sea Gate, the rock arch the tide runs through twice a day. Nearest: city Tử Điện Thành (180 km), town Hòa Phong Trấn (225 km), beast lair Quần Hầu Lĩnh (226 km). Wood-qi.
places.imagined: Slack water at midday: a bridal boat decked in red cloth rows slowly through the arch, with the whole village on the rocks watching.
places.subject: The place: Hải Môn Thôn, the Sea Gate Village, beside a great natural rock arch. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at midday at slack tide; a river runs through green farmland hills to a deep bay of the sea at the upper left, small farm plots on the slope. The village: about forty small grey-tile houses along the shore and the slope behind, each with nets on poles and a few upturned boats; a tide-clock post on the beach with a painted scale; a small shrine, a market shed, a net-loft and about twenty-five fishing boats drawn up on the sand or waiting in the sheltered water on the inner side of the arch. Signature element: the Sea Gate, a huge natural arch of pale grey rock striped with brown, about forty paces high and thirty wide, standing across a narrow channel at the end of the headland so the whole sea passes through it; at slack water the surface in the arch is calm and glassy, but white tide-lines on the rocks show the rush twice a day; a single boat, decked in red cloth, rows through it carrying a bride and groom in red with a few relatives, while on the nearby rocks a crowd of about eighty tiny villagers watch. Life at scale: a small village that lives by a rock and the tide. Light: bright midday light from the upper left, the arch's shadow a dark blue ellipse on the water.

places.name: Tân Khẩu Thôn
places.size: A refugee village of about 180 people: about 40 houses facing the sea and joined landward into one long blank windowless wall about 400 m long, with about 20 boats.
places.where: Region 12 (the bay), grassland coast at 0.01 km, a port at a harbour mouth. Held by Lạc Hà Tông; founded in 805 by refugees from Vô Định Thành after the battle on the plain, who never speak of it. Miasma still lies by Vô Định Thành. Nearest: hot spring Vong Ưu Tuyền (79 km), town Hòa Phong Trấn (202 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Dusk: lamps are lit on the sea side and the long blank wall lies dark against the plain, where a child's shape is visible at the edge of a pale haze.
places.subject: The place: Tân Khẩu Thôn, the Harbour Mouth Village, a refugee village that turns its back to the land. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dusk; a straight green hilly coast with a few farm plots, the open bay lying to the north. Dark violet sky with a faint miasma haze lies low on the plain at the far edge. The village: about forty small grey-tile houses in a single long curved line along the harbour edge, all with doors and windows facing the sea; on the landward side the houses join into one continuous blank grey wall, about four hundred paces long, without a window or a door, plastered in plain grey, higher than the houses, turned against the plain; at each end a narrow gap with a small guarded gate; a small harbour of about twenty boats, a shed, a quay with lamp-posts, and one plain hall with a bell. Signature element: the blank wall, a grim grey barrier, and, at a distance beyond it, on the plain in the thin haze, three tiny children's figures dared to the edge of the miasma, one pointing, with an adult running toward them from a gate; the village lamps glow warm on the sea side. Life at scale: a small, taut, silent community. Gulls sit along the harbour wall and a net hangs drying over a skiff. Light: low gold-rose dusk light from the upper left, long shadow of the wall across the grass, the pale haze menacing.
